body.statement:
For every finite rational input \(\mathsf{Data}\),
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{a valid finite }\mathsf{GapCert}\text{ exists}.
\]
There is an exact terminating construction and verifier using real-closed-field
quantifier elimination, exact polynomial reduction, and exact sign
determination on \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\); outward-rounded rational
arithmetic is used only for the two objective enclosures.  If \(d\) is the
total number of real variables in the two standard-form programs,
\(B\) is the binary input length, and
\(\Delta=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}>0\), put
\[
 \log_2^+(1/\Delta)=\max\{0,\log_2(1/\Delta)\}.
\]
For a universal constant \(\kappa_{\mathrm{alg}}>0\), the construction and
interval separation use
at most
\[
 \bigl(B+\lceil\log_2^+(1/\Delta)\rceil+1\bigr)^{2^{\kappa_{\mathrm{alg}}d}}
\]
bit operations.  The equivalence and algorithm require neither unique
optimizers, positive donor weights, independent predictor columns, ordinary
Slater feasibility, nor strict complementarity, and they cover tight and
collapsed Lorentz-cone blocks.  The positive part in the displayed complexity
bound is necessary because the model imposes no normalization forcing
\(\Delta\le1\).
body.proof_tex:
Write \(P_s\) for the standard-form program in
\texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}, and interpret its value in
\([0,+\infty]\).  We first settle feasibility and attainment, including the
boundary case in which a donor simplex is empty.

For \(0\leq h\leq K\), the definition of the donor sets gives
\[
 D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}, \tag{6}
\]
because \(T_i>T_j+K\) implies \(T_i>T_j+h\).  If the nested program is
feasible, then its horizon-\(K\) coordinate supplies an element of
\(\Delta(D_{jK})\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), so each \(D_{jK}\) is
nonempty.  Choosing one point of each such simplex at every horizon gives a
deep-feasible weight array.  Conversely, (6) embeds every deep-feasible
weight array into the nested feasible set.  All norm epigraphs admit finite
slacks once weights have been chosen.  Hence
\[
 P_{\mathrm{nested}}\text{ is feasible}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 P_{\mathrm{deep}}\text{ is feasible}. \tag{7}
\]
If these programs are infeasible, both values are \(+\infty\), so their
strict inequality is false.  A valid \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) is also impossible:
its \(y_N\) would be nested feasible and its \(y^\circ\) would be deep
feasible.  Thus the asserted equivalence already holds in the infeasible
case.

Suppose henceforth that the equivalent conditions in (7) hold.  Eliminating
the norm epigraph variables at a fixed weight array gives
\[
 G_s(w):=\max_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{
 L\left\|x_j-\sum_i w_{jh,i}x_i\right\|_2
 +\delta+z_B\left\|R_Qa_{jh}(w)\right\|_2
 \right\}. \tag{8}
\]
Indeed, the smallest feasible values of \(u_{jh}\) and \(v_{jh}\) are the
two norms in (8), and the smallest feasible \(g\) is their displayed finite
maximum.  Every nonempty finite-dimensional donor simplex is compact, so the
finite product \(\mathcal F_s\) is compact.  The affine maps, Euclidean
norms, and finite maximum in (8) are continuous.  Therefore
\[
 \Gamma_s=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}G_s(w)<+\infty, \tag{9}
\]
and the minimum is attained.  Choosing the norm values, the maximizing
epigraph value, and the corresponding nonnegative slacks restores an
attained optimizer of \(P_s\).  This argument neither requires a unique
minimizer nor divides by a donor weight or a predictor Gram matrix.

Assume first that
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}},
 \qquad
 \Delta:=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}>0. \tag{10}
\]
By (9), choose a nested primal optimizer \(y_N^*\).  The cone
\(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}\) is a finite product of closed orthants,
Lorentz cones, and zero cones, and hence is a finite-dimensional closed
convex cone.  Its affine space
\[
 H_D:=\{y:B_{\mathrm{deep}}y=d_{\mathrm{deep}}\}
\]
meets the cone by (7).  Apply
\texttt{lem:facial-reduction-relative-strong-duality} to this conic affine
system.  It gives a finite strict facial-reduction chain
\[
 \mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}=F_0\supsetneq F_1\supsetneq\cdots
 \supsetneq F_r=F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}, \tag{11}
\]
and a point
\[
 y^\circ\in H_D\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{12}
\]
Each strict inclusion lowers dimension, so
\(r\leq\dim\mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}\leq d\).

For completeness, the affine multiplier form required by
\texttt{def:facial-dual} follows by elementary finite-dimensional linear
algebra.  At step \(k\), the orthogonal exposing functional \(z_k\)
annihilates the affine space \(H_D\); in particular it annihilates its
direction space \(\ker B_{\mathrm{deep}}\).  Hence
\[
 z_k\in(\ker B_{\mathrm{deep}})^\perp
       =\operatorname{range}(B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}),
\]
so \(z_k=B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta_k\) for some \(\eta_k\).  For any
\(y_0\in H_D\), annihilation of the affine space then gives
\[
 0=z_k^{\top}y_0
   =\eta_k^{\top}B_{\mathrm{deep}}y_0
   =\eta_k^{\top}d_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\]
Thus the chain satisfies every exposing identity in
\texttt{def:facial-dual}.  Since the deep value is finite by (9), the same
cited lemma supplies an attained facial-dual optimizer \(\lambda_D^*\) with
\[
 c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*
 \in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*,
 \qquad
 d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*
 =\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{13}
\]

We next show that the real objects in (11)--(13) can be replaced by exact
real-algebraic objects through a terminating procedure, without imposing a
nondegeneracy condition.  The required cone and face relations are
semialgebraic.  Orthant membership is a list of linear weak inequalities, a
zero cone is specified by linear equalities, and
\[
 (t,z)\in\mathcal L_q
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 t\geq0\ \text{ and }\ t^2-\sum_{\nu=1}^{q-1}z_\nu^2\geq0. \tag{14}
\]
The faces of an orthant are its coordinate faces.  A proper nonzero face of a
Lorentz cone is a ray: two noncollinear nonzero boundary points have an
interior midpoint by the strict triangle inequality, and a face containing
an interior point is the whole cone.  Finally, every face of a product cone
is a product of faces.  To see this last assertion, decompose a point of the
face into its block-supported cone components; the face property puts every
component in the face, and closure under addition gives the converse product
inclusion.  Thus an orthant face is encoded by zero/free coordinate labels,
and a Lorentz face is encoded as full, zero, or a ray with a normalized
boundary generator.  Membership, relative-interior membership, dual-face
membership, and equality
\(F_k=F_{k-1}\cap z_k^\perp\) are consequently finite Boolean combinations
of polynomial sign conditions.  Binary labels can themselves be imposed by
\(e(e-1)=0\), so no enumeration of exponentially many cases is required.

For each \(0\leq r\leq d\), form the following first-order formula
\(\Psi_r\) over the rationals.  Its existential variables are a chain of
length \(r\), its face parameters and exposing multipliers, a point
\(y^\circ\) satisfying (12), a nested feasible point \(y_N\), and a feasible
facial-dual point \(\lambda_D\).  Its conditions are exactly those in
\texttt{def:facial-dual}, together with
\[
 \begin{split}
 &c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N
   \leq c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}\widetilde y_N
   \quad\text{for every nested-feasible }\widetilde y_N,\\
 &d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D
   \geq d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\widetilde\lambda_D
   \quad\text{for every facial-dual-feasible }
      \widetilde\lambda_D,\\
 &c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N
   <d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D.
 \end{split} \tag{15}
\]
The two universal competitor families in (15) may be placed in one universal
quantifier block after the existential block.  Conditions (10)--(13) and
nested attainment show that at least one \(\Psi_r\) is true.  Conversely, a
solution of a \(\Psi_r\) has
\[
 c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N=\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}},
 \qquad
 d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}, \tag{16}
\]
where the second equality uses (12) and relative-interior strong duality.
Thus the finite disjunction \(\bigvee_{r=0}^d\Psi_r\) is true if and only if
the strict inequality in (10) is true.

All multiplier quantifiers can be bounded in dimension even when the equality
rows are redundant.  For a program with \(n\) primal variables, apply exact
rational row reduction to
\[
 \mathcal R:\eta\longmapsto
 \bigl(B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta,
       d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta\bigr)
 \in\mathbb R^{n+1}. \tag{17}
\]
Choose columns whose images form a basis of
\(\operatorname{range}\mathcal R\).  Every multiplier has another
representative supported on those columns with the same two images in (17),
and there are at most \(n+1\leq d+1\) selected columns.  Both the exposing
identities and facial-dual feasibility and objective depend only on those two
images.  The full certificate multiplier is recovered by inserting zeros in
the unselected positions.  Therefore the existential block, including at
most \(d\) faces and exposures, has \(O(d^2)\) real variables; the combined
universal competitor block has \(O(d)\) variables.  The number of polynomial
atoms and their coefficient bit lengths are polynomial in the explicit input
length \(B\), and their degrees are bounded by a universal constant after
introducing standard auxiliary variables.  Clearing rational denominators
turns them into the integer-coefficient sign conditions required by
\texttt{lem:effective-real-algebraic-elimination}.

That cited effective theorem now gives a total exact decision procedure for
the disjunction and, whenever it is true, real-algebraic sample values for all
existential variables.  Denote the sampled values again by
\(y_N,\lambda_D,y^\circ,z_k,\eta_k\).  By (15)--(16), the algebraic numbers
\[
 p_N:=c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N,
 \qquad
 q_D:=d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D
\]
satisfy
\[
 p_N=\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}},
 \qquad q_D=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}},
 \qquad q_D-p_N=\Delta>0. \tag{18}
\]
Exact real-algebraic arithmetic supplies square-free polynomial
representations and isolating intervals for \(p_N\) and \(q_D\).  Repeated
rational bisection, with exact polynomial sign determination at each rational
midpoint, produces outward rational enclosures \(I_N\) and \(I_D\).  Once
each interval has length less than \(\Delta/3\), (18) implies
\[
 \sup I_N
 <p_N+\frac{\Delta}{3}
 <q_D-\frac{\Delta}{3}
 <\inf I_D. \tag{19}
\]
Hence the adaptive exact test \(\sup I_N<\inf I_D\) eventually succeeds,
although the algorithm need not know \(\Delta\) in advance.  The sampled
chain, algebraic points and multipliers, and the two intervals then form the
finite \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) of \texttt{def:gap-certificate}.  This proves the
forward implication.  The reverse implication is exactly
\texttt{prop:strict-gap-sufficient}.  It also shows that, when the exact
decision procedure returns false, no valid certificate exists.

We give the promised bit bound.  By
\texttt{lem:effective-real-algebraic-elimination}, a formula with the fixed
two-block pattern above, polynomial input size, and block dimensions bounded
by a polynomial in \(d\) can be decided and sampled in at most
\[
 (B+1)^{d^{c_0}} \tag{20}
\]
bit operations after increasing a universal constant \(c_0\); the same
envelope bounds the degrees, coefficient heights, exact algebraic arithmetic,
and sign determination.  There is a universal \(\kappa_0>0\) such that
\(d^{c_0}\leq2^{\kappa_0d}\) for every positive integer \(d\).  To force the
absolute interval lengths below \(\min\{1,\Delta\}/3\), bisection needs, in
addition to the algebraic representation length, at most a polynomial number
of operations in
\[
 \ell_\Delta:=\left\lceil\log_2^+(1/\Delta)\right\rceil+1.
\]
Polynomial evaluation at the resulting rational endpoints has bit cost
polynomial in the representation length and \(\ell_\Delta\).  Absorbing
these polynomial factors and (20) by increasing a universal constant yields
\[
 \bigl(B+\lceil\log_2^+(1/\Delta)\rceil+1\bigr)^{
       2^{\kappa_{\mathrm{alg}}d}}. \tag{21}
\]
The verifier checks the face descriptions and the first-order face identities
by exact real-closed-field decision, reduces every displayed affine equality
to an exact polynomial identity in \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\), and uses
exact sign determination for (14), orthant signs, relative-interior signs,
and facial-dual membership.  Outward-rounded rational arithmetic is used only
to enclose the two objectives and to check the strict rational comparison in
(19).

The positive part in (21) cannot be removed under the stated input class.
Indeed, consider \(N=4\), \(T=2\), \(K=1\), and one treated unit \(j\) with
\(T_j=1\), one unit \(e\) with \(T_e=2\), and two never-treated units
\(d_1,d_2\).  Then
\[
 D_{j0}=\{e,d_1,d_2\},
 \qquad D_{j1}=\{d_1,d_2\},
 \qquad \mathcal J=\{j\}.
\]
Take \(p=1\), \(x_i=0\), and \(L=\delta=0\).  Fix the supplied admissible
positive rational \(z_B\) and its tail certificates.  For any positive
rational \(c\), let \(R_Q\) be diagonal, with entry \(c\) on every
time-\(1\) row cell and entry \(c/10\) on every time-\(2\) row cell.  This is
a full-rank rational factor with covariance eigenvalues in the legal band
\([c^2/100,c^2]\).  The cells in the two rows have different calendar times
and hence are distinct.  For \(q\) equal-variance donors, Cauchy--Schwarz
gives
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^q w_i^2\geq\frac1q,
\]
with equality at uniform weights.  Therefore the minimized squared noise
norms at horizons zero and one are, respectively,
\[
 \begin{array}{c|cc}
 &h=0&h=1\\ \hline
 \mathrm{nested}&4c^2/3&3c^2/200\\
 \mathrm{deep}&3c^2/2&3c^2/200.
 \end{array}
\]
Because the two weight coordinates vary independently and the objective is
their maximum, (8) yields
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}=z_Bc\sqrt{4/3},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}=z_Bc\sqrt{3/2},
\]
and hence
\[
 \Delta=z_Bc\bigl(\sqrt{3/2}-\sqrt{4/3}\bigr).
\]
This gap exceeds one for all sufficiently large rational \(c\).  Thus the
model supplies no normalization forcing \(\Delta\leq1\); using
\(\log_2(1/\Delta)\) without its positive part could make the alleged
precision allowance negative even though reading and verifying the finite
input still has positive cost.

None of the arguments above invokes uniqueness, positivity of every donor
weight, predictor-column independence, ordinary Slater feasibility, or strict
complementarity.  Zero weights are ordinary orthant-boundary points,
redundant predictors only repeat polynomial conditions, and (14) together
with the explicit face encoding includes both ray faces and the zero face of
every tight or collapsed Lorentz block.  The equivalence and the construction
are finite-sample, exact statements; no limiting argument is used.
